slides.title: 5 snow and ice myths to drop before the first big storm

slides.myth: Rock salt works no matter how cold it gets.
slides.fact: Regular rock salt slows way down once the pavement drops below about 15°F. Use a deicer rated for the cold, or sand for grip.
slides.source: Minnesota Pollution Control Agency, U of Minnesota

slides.myth: More salt melts the ice faster.
slides.fact: About 12 ounces, one coffee mug, treats a 20-foot driveway or 10 sidewalk squares. Shovel first. Extra salt just ends up in local water.

slides.myth: Salting a brand-new concrete driveway is fine.
slides.fact: Concrete pros say to keep deicers off it for the first year. Young concrete scales and flakes more easily. Use sand for traction.

slides.myth: Ice dams mean your gutters are clogged.
slides.fact: Ice dams start in the attic. Heat leaking from the house melts roof snow, and it refreezes at the cold edge. Air sealing and insulation fix it.

slides.myth: Just chip the ice dam off with a hammer.
slides.fact: Never chop through the ice down to the shingles, and never use a blowtorch. In a pinch, hose channels through it with tap water on a warm day.
